_comment: Permission rules the firm has WITHDRAWN. firm-install only ever unions rules into a project's
settings.json, so a project installed from an older version keeps a retired rule forever unless
something removes it. `firm-install --migrate` is that something, and firm-doctor FAILS while a
retired rule is still present — a warning would leave the hole open in every existing project.
Honesty note: deleting these from `allow` is the real fix. The matching `deny` entries in
.claude/settings.json are belt-and-braces against the specific known-bad reads, NOT a sandbox —
Bash pattern matching cannot enumerate every way to read a file. The dev-container and scoped,
read-only credentials remain the actual containment. See docs/ENFORCEMENT.md.

retired.reason: Read-tool deny rules (Read(./.env), Read(~/.ssh/**), Read(~/.aws/**), Read(~/.codex/auth.json)) bind ONLY the Read tool. An allow-listed `cat` reads straight around every one of them.
retired.replacement: Use the Read tool, which the deny rules actually bind. Ad-hoc `cat` now falls through to the normal permission prompt.

retired.reason: Same read-around as `cat`, aimed at JSON credential stores (~/.claude.json, ~/.codex/auth.json, cloud credential files).
retired.replacement: Read the file with the Read tool. jq on the firm's own ledger artifacts now prompts once rather than being blanket-granted.
